title: Generic ranks of completed differentials over reduced equidimensional algebras
statement:
Let $k$ be a perfect field and $S$ a reduced finite-type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], pure of dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-pure-dimension]. Let $\mathfrak m$ be a maximal ideal with residue field $k$, let $A=S_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], let $R=\widehat A$ be its maximal-ideal completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and suppose $R$ is reduced. Put $N=\Omega^1_{A/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and $M_R=N\otimes_A R$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. Then $S$ is geometrically reduced over $k$ (its tensor product with every field extension of $k$ is reduced), and every generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}S$ belongs to its smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], with local topological dimension $d$. For every minimal prime $\mathfrak a$ of $A$, $A_{\mathfrak a}$ is a field and $\dim_{A_{\mathfrak a}}(N\otimes_A A_{\mathfrak a})=d$. For every minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, its contraction $\mathfrak a=\mathfrak p\cap A$ is minimal in $A$, $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a field, and $A_{\mathfrak a}\to R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a field extension. In particular
$$\dim_{R_{\mathfrak p}}(M_R\otimes_R R_{\mathfrak p})=d.$$
More generally, for any field $L$ and $k$-algebra map $\theta:R\to L$ whose restriction to $A$ factors through a generic point in its smooth $d$-dimensional locus, $\dim_L(N\otimes_A L)=d$.

source.place: Agent-formulated generic-rank consequence of Tag 056V (lemma-geometrically-reduced-dense-smooth-open) and Tag 0A21 (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic), with algebra.tex Tags 00HS (lemma-flat-going-down), 00EU (lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring) and morphisms.tex Tag 02G1 (lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free). Returned parent proof Steps 3--4 and the rank assertion in Step 9.

proof.text: Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}S$. The finite-type hypothesis gives that $S$ is Noetherian and $X$ has finitely many irreducible components, by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$; hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] makes $S$ finitely presented over $k$. For every field extension $k'/k$, both $S$ and $k'$ are reduced, so [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-reduced-tensor] says $S\otimes_k k'$ is reduced. This is precisely the asserted geometric reducedness. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff], this also says that $X$ and each $\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_k k')$ are reduced schemes, as required for Step 2.

By [lem-pur-geometrically-reduced-dense-smooth-open], the smooth open $U\subset X$ is dense. Write the finitely many components as $C_i$ with generic points $\eta_i$. The open $X\setminus\bigcup_{j\ne i}C_j$ contains $\eta_i$ and is contained in $C_i$; density gives a point of $U$ in it. Thus $U\cap C_i$ is nonempty open in $C_i$, and contains $\eta_i$ by the defining generic-point property. Apply [lem-sbc-equidimensional-open-local-dimension] with $Y=O=X$ and $n=d$: pure dimension is exactly its component-dimension hypothesis. Consequently every $\eta_i$ is smooth and has local topological dimension $d$. This dimension is the infimum of dimensions of open neighbourhoods, not the Krull dimension of the generic local ring.

Fix a minimal prime $\mathfrak a\subset A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization], its contraction $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak m$ in $S$ is minimal: a smaller prime is also contained in $\mathfrak m$ and would extend to a smaller prime in $A$. The ring $A$ is reduced by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-preserves-reduced], so $F=A_{\mathfrak a}$ is a field by [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field]. Successive fractions identify $F=S_{\mathfrak q}$: elements outside $\mathfrak m$ are already outside $\mathfrak q$, and localizing $A$ further at $\mathfrak a$ inverts exactly the remaining elements outside $\mathfrak q$. By Step 2, $\eta=\mathfrak q$ lies in the smooth open $U$; apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-differentials-free-rank-fibre-dimension] to the smooth $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ at $\eta$. As $\kappa$ of the point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is $k$, the fibre is $U$ itself, and $\dim_\eta U=\dim_\eta X=d$ (Step 2), opens of $U$ being opens of $X$. This gives an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq U$ containing $\eta$ with $\Omega_{B/k}\cong B^{\oplus d}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], localizing $B$ at the prime of $\eta$ gives the same ring $S_{\mathfrak q}=F$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] to $S\to A$, $A\to F$, and $B\to F$. These canonical maps identify $N\otimes_A F$ with $\Omega_{F/k}$ and then with $\Omega_{B/k}\otimes_B F\cong F^{\oplus d}$; all send a differential to the differential of its image. Hence its $F$-dimension is $d$. For each localization used here, the module comparison $Q\otimes_C T^{-1}C\cong T^{-1}Q$ sends $q\otimes c/t$ to $cq/t$ and has inverse $q/t\mapsto q\otimes1/t$; the fraction and balancing relations make these inverse maps well-defined.

The ring $A=S_{\mathfrak m}$ is Noetherian by Step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat] makes $A\to R$ flat. Let $\mathfrak p$ be minimal in $R$ and put $\mathfrak a=\mathfrak p\cap A$. For any prime $\mathfrak b\subseteq\mathfrak a$, [lem-sc-flat-going-down] lifts the inclusion to a prime $\mathfrak p'\subseteq\mathfrak p$ contracting to $\mathfrak b$. Minimality forces $\mathfrak p'=\mathfrak p$, hence $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak a$. Thus $\mathfrak a$ is minimal in $A$. The reducedness hypothesis on $R$ and [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field] make $E=R_{\mathfrak p}$ a field. For $s\notin\mathfrak a$, its image lies outside $\mathfrak p$ and is invertible in $E$, so fractions define $A_{\mathfrak a}\to E$. This is a unital map of nonzero fields and is injective, because its kernel is a proper ideal of a field.

For $F=A_{\mathfrak a}$ and $E=R_{\mathfrak p}$ from Step 4, the tensor maps give
$$(N\otimes_A R)\otimes_R E\cong N\otimes_A E\cong (N\otimes_A F)\otimes_F E.$$
The first sends $(n\otimes r)\otimes e$ to $n\otimes re$ with inverse $n\otimes e\mapsto(n\otimes1)\otimes e$; the second sends $(n\otimes f)\otimes e$ to $n\otimes fe$, with inverse $n\otimes e\mapsto(n\otimes1)\otimes e$. These formulas respect the balancing relations. Step 3 identifies $N\otimes_A F$ with $F^{\oplus d}$. Tensor this isomorphism and its inverse with $E$; the coordinate maps $F^{\oplus d}\otimes_F E\rightleftarrows E^{\oplus d}$ send $e_i\otimes e$ to the vector with entry $e$ at $i$, and a vector $(c_i)$ to $\sum_i e_i\otimes c_i$. They are inverse, including for $d=0$. This proves the completed rank formula.

source.place: Section 00CV (section-tensor-product), tensor balancing relations; elementary scalar-extension calculation

proof.text: Finally suppose $\theta:R\to L$ has the stated factorization on $A$. Thus the $A$-action on $L$ factors through the generic local field $F=A_{\mathfrak a}$ at the specified smooth point of dimension $d$. The calculation in Step 3 gives $N\otimes_A F\cong F^{\oplus d}$. Apply the same tensor formulas as Step 5 with $E=L$ to obtain $N\otimes_A L\cong L^{\oplus d}$ and dimension $d$. Only this factorization of the $A$-action is used; neither injectivity of $\theta$ nor any assertion that $\Omega_{R/k}$ is a completed differential module is required.
